evaluator: Independent Codex holdout evaluator using a fictionalized Margaret Morse analytical lens; not Margaret Morse, not speaking for her, and providing no endorsement
evidence: Within one click from the homepage, /about explicitly names the through-line as “Systems people can inhabit” and connects Open House, WOW List, Sunday Dinner/196, NYC Artist Coalition, and source-backed team memory across artistic, civic, technical, and social practice.

At least three distinct continuities are legible: Harry J. Epstein turns customer language and institutional knowledge into maintained commerce workflows; FairRentNYC joins public websites, facilitated meetings, town halls, source maps, and decision memory; Sunday Dinner/196 turns invitations, food, welcome, artist support, documentation, and follow-up into repeatable participation infrastructure.

The FairRentNYC case makes inhabitation concrete by describing the website as only one part of the room, alongside a coalition working session and public town hall. It distinguishes Jamie’s implementation, facilitation, documentation, and policy-communications contributions from the coalition’s collective accomplishments.

The Sunday Dinner/196 page centers hospitality and care: orientation around an artist’s actual needs, preparation for independent access, continued availability, food, welcome, introductions, minimal continuity records, and protection of participant context.

WOW List connects social language to technical form through collaboratively editable natural-language posts and followable keyword communities. It credits Richard Caceres as co-founder and co-builder, credits organizers and participants, connects the product to Sunday Dinner and later organizing, and labels 2017 counts as historical rather than current activity.

Jamie’s target role remains conspicuous on /, /about, individual case studies, and /resume: Technical Project Manager, Product Operations, and Implementation. Each case names a concrete responsibility, usable outcome, evidence surface, and role-fit translation.

Collective credit and causal limits are unusually explicit: FairRentNYC says policy outcomes and movements remain collective; event responses are not attendance; shared-account authorship is unattributed; Sunday Dinner names Julia Fredenburg as co-organizer where supported; Open House and WOW List reject sole-authorship implications.

Privacy and consent boundaries are visible rather than implicit. The Sunday Dinner/196 page withholds participant identities, contacts, attendance histories, correspondence, addresses, access instructions, proposals, and unapproved images; FairRentNYC withholds strategy, legal-review context, stakeholder lists, and unapproved quotations.

Historical and current states are carefully separated. WOW List’s 2017 production snapshot is not presented as current adoption, its present surface is described as a noindex tester threshold rather than a restored calendar, and Source-Backed Team Memory is labeled an early method rather than production SaaS.

Source integrity is supported by visible notes that state what each source establishes and does not establish. The lab also exposes a concrete correction trace changing CallNYC’s date from an earlier claim to 2016 and propagating that correction across public surfaces.
gaps: The Harry J. Epstein 2x-revenue contribution remains publicly summarized rather than independently auditable because detailed analytics and revenue records are intentionally private.

The Sunday Dinner/196 scale is appropriately bounded: public milestones and aggregate controls do not establish unique participants, exact attendance, or an independently audited count of every gathering.

The displayed Sunday Dinner photograph has unresolved creator attribution; the page discloses that limitation and describes the image as cleared for bounded portfolio display, but fuller creator credit remains open.
WOW List’s contemporary governance, moderation, retention, contribution model, and complete relaunch remain open product work.

Source-Backed Team Memory demonstrates a method and correction practice, not a completed external client pilot. These are disclosed limitations rather than material ambiguities in the portfolio’s through-line.
safety_findings: No blocking public-safety or source-integrity problem was observed on the reviewed public pages.

The reviewed surface does not visibly expose raw participant records, private correspondence, access instructions, credentials, private analytics, legal-review materials, or sensitive stakeholder lists.
Claims involving attendance, social-media populations, policy outcomes, revenue, authorship, and causation carry visible qualifications and stopping conditions.
Collective projects retain collaborator or community credit, and absent or unresolved attribution is disclosed rather than silently assigned.
The lab preserves human review and correction gates: AI drafts, humans review, and protected material remains outside public memory.
This holdout judgment is observational only and does not authorize publication, deployment, indexing, testimonial use, or release of protected material.
recommendation: Pass PR-015 for the candidate bound to the stated SHA-256. Preserve the existing public-safe labels, source boundaries, collective-credit language, historical/current distinctions, noindex staging posture, correction paths, and separate human authorization gates.
